teenKit.tldr: A 68-year-old man survived an impossible blood pH of 6.78 caused by a severe reaction to diabetes medication, showcasing how extreme medical intervention can temporarily pause human cellular machinery.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how drugs interact with our cellular power plants helps modern medicine save lives from catastrophic biochemical crashes that used to be considered completely fatal.
keyTakeaways: An arterial blood pH of 6.78 is normally far past the point of biological survival, where proteins and enzymes should unravel and die.
Metformin-Associated Lactic Acidosis (MALA) occurs when a common diabetes drug triggers a massive buildup of acid and lactate in the bloodstream.
Advanced treatments like EXTRIP dialysis and a molecular-level understanding of cellular machinery can sometimes pull patients back from the brink of absolute cellular failure.
